transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Natarajan (Arborlane - Procurement), Ethan Cole (Arborlane - Security), Lena Park (Arborlane - VP Eng)

Summary:
- Commercial acceptance / procurement handoff from AE to internal procurement team; focus on MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA metrics, pricing and pilot acceptance criteria.
- Technical preflight: Redwood SE to run a staging benchmark that mirrors Arborlane's typical 1-3s latency-sensitive calls and large batch embedding workload.
- Security/compliance: customer requested SOC2 artifacts, encryption at rest KMS options, and a note on audit-log retention.

Topics covered:
- MSA redline focus areas (liability cap, data residency, IP carve-outs)
- DPA specifics (processing vs controller, subprocessor list, deletion timelines)
- SLA: uptime, P99 latency target, credits flow and escalation path
- Pricing approval lanes (hosted vs dedicated capacity) and commitment thresholds
- Pilot acceptance criteria and timeline to go-live

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for taking the time, um this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, i'll run through the handoff and make sure we capture procurement ask, also carlos is with me for the technical bits.
[00:12] Priya: hey thanks Maya, we've got procurement and security here, lena's joining to talk scoping too. main thing for us is to understand redlines so we can route internally.
[00:20] Carlos: yep hi all, quick intro i'm Carlos Ortiz, solutions engineer. i'll be doing the staging runs and the technical acceptance checklist.
[00:28] Lena: quick note — timeline wise we'd like to get pilots started by the end of the month if procurement can move fast.

[02:03] Priya: for procurement, the standard checklist — we need the MSA with redlines, the DPA, and confirmation of who the subproces-sors are. also PO flow and an invoice path. any special escrow or data escrow you support?
[02:18] Maya: for escalation — we don't do escrow by default, we can discuss exec-level options, but standard is we provide the DPA and subprocessor list. i'll put the current subprocessor list in the packet.
[02:35] Ethan: on security, can you confirm key management options — customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed? and how are logs retained and where?
[02:48] Carlos: good question. we support both. for Private deployments you can bring your KMS (HSM/KMS integration) and for Hosted we have BYOK options via KMS integrations. audit logs can be exported to your S3/CloudWatch with configurable retention, default retention is 90 days but you can request longer for an enterprise package.
[03:20] Priya: liability cap and indemnity t's are usually a hang-up — we need clarity on cap and any insurance references, does redwood accept typical enterprise carving?
[03:36] Maya: we usually start with our standard cap at [company standard], but we are open to limited exceptions for enterprise deals; i'll flag the clauses i expect we'll get pushback on. i'll also include a one-page summary of exceptions for quick legal review.

[06:00] Lena: on the SLA, our platform needs p99 response under 500ms for short text gen calls; is that realistic on hosted or do we need dedicated?
[06:14] Carlos: 500ms p99 at production scale is tough on shared hosted unless you choose the low-latency model profile and reserve burst capacity. For predictable p99 we recommend Dedicated capacity. the tradeoff is cost. we can run a benchmark that mirrors your request mix — short gen + sporadic long-context + batch embeddings — and give you a realistic SLO table.
[06:45] Ethan: and if a dedicated pool is down, what's the fallback? do we have automatic model fallback to lower-cost variants?
[06:55] Carlos: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible model variant in another pool or region — you can configure failover policies, with optional canary or thundering herd protections.

[09:10] Priya: pricing question — procurement is trying to build out a 12-month projection. can you provide hosted per-token pricing and a committed-dedicated tier price so we can compare?
[09:25] Maya: sure — i'll include a pricing worksheet with three lanes: self-serve hosted, committed dedicated with monthly commit tiers, and private deployment (license + support). note that committed tiers have lower per-token plus reserved GPU pricing. i'll also call out egress and KMS fee assumptions so your finops team can model TCO.

[11:50] Ethan: on DPA deletion timelines: if a user requests deletion, what's the timeline for purging logs and model input traces?
[12:01] Carlos: typical timeline is 30 days for immediate deletion requests for user-level data in hosted, with longer windows for backups up to 90 days; for dedicated/private we can tighten those windows contractually since data partitioning is stronger. i'll capture precise wording.

[14:40] Lena: pilot acceptance criteria — we need pass/fail metrics. if the pilot fails due to latency or accuracy regressions, what's the remediation path?
[14:55] Maya: suggestion — define a 3-week pilot with 1) latency SLA band, 2) cost per 1k tokens threshold, 3) basic accuracy checks on your sample prompts. if there's a regression we set a 2-week remediation where SEs work to tune batching/quantization or recommend model variants. if unresolved, you can opt out of commitment.

[18:12] Priya: procurement sign path — i will need the redlined MSA back with a short note on exceptions. do you have a template PO format we accept?
[18:23] Maya: yes i will attach our PO instructions — we accept standard POs referencing CRM-ARBL-2025-0912. we'll also include the billing contact and bank details; for invoicing cadence we can do monthly or quarterly net-30.

[21:40] Carlos: a couple technical caveats — we saw transcription artifacts in one of the earlier demos where some long-contexts created high memory pressure; for your long-chat workload we recommend the optimized kv cache path and a model profile with quantized kernels. for the staging run i'll spin up the quantized variant plus a 16k context run.

[24:05] Ethan: do you provide SOC2 attestation? can we see recent reports or WIPs?
[24:12] Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II is available for customers under an NDA; i'll attach the assertion and the compliance packet. also pen-test summaries and a list of third-party auditors.

[28:00] Lena: on private deployment — does the private package include the control plane or is it customer-managed? and what about upgrade windows?
[28:15] Carlos: private includes the control plane optionally federated: you can choose a customer-managed control plane with our connectors or a Redwood-managed control plane inside your VPC. upgrades are scheduled with maintenance windows; for sensitive customers we agree to fixed release windows and a rollback plan.

[31:30] Priya: procurement needs a single line for the SLA commitments that legal can see quickly — uptime, p99, credits, and the escalation contact.
[31:45] Maya: i'll create an SLA summary page listing uptime percentage, p99 lat targets by model class, credit calculation formulas, and contact ladder. also i'll flag the customer-specific escalation emails.

[35:00] Priya: about DPA and subprocessors — i'd like to see a list and any planned future subprocessor additions so we can pre-clear them.
[35:12] Maya: understood — i'll include current subprocessor list and the notification cadence for adding ones in the future. typical approach is 30-day notice for new subprocessors.

[38:44] Carlos: quick note about benchmarking results we will provide — i'll attach a spreadsheet with raw runs and a summarized SLO map. the sheet will include latency histograms and cost per 1k token at the test concurrency.

[41:20] Priya: internal timelines — procurement wants sign-off by 2025-11-20 to hit your pilot start date. is that realistic?
[41:33] Maya: yes it's realistic if legal can triage the redlines quickly; that's why i'll include a one-page exception summary to speed review.

[43:50] Lena: if we move to dedicated, what does onboarding look like operationally? will we need training for our on-call?
[44:02] Carlos: we provide an onboarding package: runbook, incident playbooks, token-level cost dashboards, and a 2-hour runbook workshop for on-call teams. we also hand over tracing hooks for your APM.

[46:05] Maya: okay great, let's recap next steps — i'll send: redline package (MSA+DPA), pricing worksheet, SLA summary. carlos will run the staging benchmark and share sheet. ethan to send the compliance artifact request list, priya to confirm procurement owners.
[46:25] Priya: sounds good, we'll aim to have internal legal review complete by 11/18 and procurement sign-off by 11/20.
[46:35] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the technical run review. thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
